title: Tenant validation and closure playbook - draft
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft intended for Customer Success and SRE to use when preparing a customer-facing closure packet for incidents where tenants are asked to assist with verification (replay/validation) before we mark the event as fully resolved. Not a formal postmortem — this sits between statuspage updates and the final technical postmortem.

TL;DR (customer-ready summary):
We experienced intermittent degraded responses for some tenant requests routed through our eu-west and us-central regions on 2026-10-21 between 03:40–04:25 UTC. Root cause: race between cache-eviction and KV-restore during autoscale; some requests hit a fallback model variant with truncated KV leading to partial outputs. We implemented a coordinated rollback and KV-resync, and traffic was routed away from affected hosts. No tenant data loss was detected.

Impact details (concise customer language):
- Who was affected: A subset of customers using long-context chat or structured output (streaming) during the window; not all requests.
- Symptoms customers saw: truncated responses, short-circuited streaming sessions, and occasional 502s followed by immediate retries.
- Duration: ~45 minutes of highest-frequency errors; residual rate anomalies for ~1 hour after mitigations.
- Data safety: No persisted user data was lost or exposed. Internal logs show no unauthorized access.

Suggested statuspage copy (short):
- 2026-10-21 04:10 UTC — Partial service degradation impacting streaming and long-context responses for a subset of tenants. We identified a cache-eviction/race condition in our autoscale path and are actively routing traffic to healthy hosts and applying a KV resync. No data loss. Updates to follow.

Suggested statuspage copy (closure):
- 2026-10-21 05:50 UTC — Services fully recovered. Mitigation actions included routing away from affected hosts, an emergency KV resync, and reverting a rollout that contributed to the race. We’ve initiated a technical postmortem and will share further details. If you continue to see anomalies, please contact support with request IDs and timestamps.

Customer closure packet (what we provide to affected tenants):
1) One-paragraph plain-language summary (copy from TL;DR).
2) Timeline of events with UTC timestamps (high-level).
3) Evidence bundle for tenant verification: list of request IDs (masked), approximate timestamps, and a signed hash (SHA256) of the server-side session logs for the time window. Explain how customers can verify the hash matches the artifact we provide.
4) Actionable verification steps (see below).
5) Offer of a replay run (opt-in) performed by Redwood or instructions for a customer-run replay in a safe, rate-limited manner.
6) Credit/compensation proposal (if applicable) and next steps for remediation.

Actionable verification steps for tenants (customer-facing, stepwise):
- Step 1: Identify any request IDs you recorded between 03:30–05:30 UTC on 2026-10-21. If you did not record request IDs, collect timestamps and sample prompts.
- Step 2: Send request IDs/timestamps to support (secure link). We will return a signed evidence package that contains the masked server session lines and a SHA256 digest.
- Step 3: Option A — Redwood replay: opt-in to have us re-run those requests against the current healthy routing plan; we will provide outputs and timing metrics. Option B — Customer replay: we provide a limited, rate‑restricted API token that replays input to the same model variant we used pre-incident; customers should follow the provided rate limits to avoid interfering with production traffic.
- Step 4: Compare outputs. If output divergence appears to be the result of earlier truncation/fallthrough we will mark items as verified and discuss remediation/credits.

Internal notes for CS agents (private checklist):
- Before sending packet: ensure SRE has produced the signed SHA256 artifact and a short timeline doc.
- Sanitize request IDs: mask tenant-specific PII, include only necessary metadata (request id, timestamp, model variant).
- For replays: confirm which model variant was used and whether upstream model fallback occurred — include in the evidence.
- Approvals: any credits > $1k require SOC/finance signoff.

Example customer email snippet (concise):
Hi <CustomerName>,
We wanted to update you about an incident on 2026-10-21 that may have impacted some of your API requests. We’ve recovered services and can provide a verification package and replay options so you can confirm there was no data loss and inspect any affected outputs. If you’d like Redwood to run a controlled replay, reply to this message and we’ll coordinate.

Common customer FAQ (draft):
Q: Was my data leaked?
A: No evidence of data exfiltration or unauthorized access. The issue was an internal cache/state race and fallback behavior that affected output completeness but not data exposure.

Q: Do I need to change my API keys?
A: No. There is no indication keys were compromised. If you prefer, we can rotate keys as a precaution — contact your account lead.

Q: How long until a final postmortem?
A: We will publish a technical postmortem within two weeks that includes mitigations, root cause analysis, and long-term fixes. This customer closure packet will be linked from that postmortem.

Next steps (internal):
- SRE: finalize root cause write-up and mitigation ticket (due 2026-11-03).
- Product/Runtime: prepare rollout freeze until fix is validated.
- CS: prepare customer packets for tenants with >1% error rate during window.
- Legal/Trust: prepare a short legal review if any partner asks for expanded evidence.

Notes on being conservative vs. being helpful:
- Provide the minimum viable evidence for customer validation (masked IDs + signed hash). Don’t dump raw logs.
- Offer Redwood-assisted replay as an easier opt-in path for less technical customers.

Open questions / items to decide before sending:
- Do we provide raw session logs to enterprise customers under NDA, or always send signed digests only? (Risk/legal)
- Credit policy: standard X% of usage during window vs. case-by-case for high-impact tenants.

Document history (short):
- 2026-10-22 initial draft by Leah Morales
- 2026-10-25 added evidence bundle workflow (Marcus Li)
- 2026-11-01 updated customer wording and closure copy (Aisha Khan)

END.
